title: Canonicalize role delimiters and gated template fingerprints during model onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: New model onboarding occasionally publishes performance profiles that do not match runtime behavior because tokenization or chat-template delimiters differ subtly between the model artifact and Redwood's canonical chat serializer. This leads to skewed per-token latency/cost numbers and intermittent template-matching failures for pinned versions.

Scope: implement a canonical role-delimiter normalizer + template-fingerprint gating step in the onboarding pipeline. If the onboarded model's tokenizer or produced role-separator byte sequence diverges from the template fingerprint used to compute published profiles, block profile publishing and surface a remediation checklist in the onboarding UI. Add smoke/regression tests and instrumentation to trace tokenizer forks and mismatches back to the model artifact (tokenizer config, merges, special tokens).
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline computes a stable 'template fingerprint' derived from tokenizer special tokens and canonical role delimiters
If fingerprint mismatch is detected, performance profiles are not published and onboarding UI shows a clear remediation path
Automated tests cover at least three tokenizer edge cases (multibyte delimiters, whitespace folding, surrogate pairs) and run in onboarding CI
Telemetry events emitted for mismatch cases with model id and fingerprint diff to aid triage
Rollout gating in runtime-1.22 ensures existing pinned models are unaffected by the new gating unless explicitly re-published

notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-03-06: Use a byte-level canonicalization step that normalizes known role tokens and collapses repeated whitespace tokens, rather than trying to fully re-tokenize prompts. This is faster and preserves existing KV cache assumptions.

Trade-off: Conservative gating may temporarily block a small number of model profiles that are nonetheless usable; we decided that blocking is preferable to publishing misleading cost/latency numbers.
Fallback plan: If customers need an immediate publish, provide a 'force publish with noted mismatch' option behind an enterprise flag with audit logging.
We will not attempt tokenizer patching during onboarding — remediation guidance will recommend model-side fixes or template aliasing in the runtime mapping layer.
implementation_notes: Fingerprint format: sha256 hex of concatenated canonical delimiter tokens + tokenizer special token list (sorted). Store fingerprint as string in model_metadata
Canonicalizer examples included in docs/ (link below). Normalize EOL sequences to LF and collapse >1 space into single space for delimiter computation
Profile publisher will compare fingerprint in model artifact with the canonicalizer output computed by onboarding runtime; mismatch stops profile publish and attaches diff to onboarding log
Telemetry event: onboarding.tokenizer_mismatch {model_id, uploader, fingerprint_model, fingerprint_runtime, reason_code}
